prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Denver. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Denver for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — I just need one quick detail: what ZIP code or Denver neighborhood are you near (e.g., Capitol Hill, Cherry Creek, Washington Park, Aurora, etc.)? Also tell me if you have dental insurance and whether you prefer a specialist (oral surgeon, periodontist, prosthodontist), a one‑stop implant center, or a lower‑cost dental school clinic. With that I’ll give a short list of specific practices to call and why each is a good choice.

Meanwhile, here’s a useful plan so you know what to ask and what types of providers to call now.

Who to call (call 2–3 of these types)
- Oral & maxillofacial surgeon (OMFS)
  - Why: Specialists in complex extractions, bone grafting, sinus lifts, sedation/general anesthesia, and surgical placement of implants — best for medically complex cases or major grafting.
- Periodontist
  - Why: Gum and bone specialists who commonly place implants and perform bone/regenerative procedures; good when periodontal health is a key factor.
- Prosthodontist (or restorative implant dentist)
  - Why: Focused on designing and restoring teeth — important for the final crown/bridge/implant prosthesis and aesthetic outcomes (especially for front teeth or full‑mouth work).
- Multidisciplinary implant center
  - Why: Teams that include surgeon + prosthodontist + lab/CBCT on‑site — convenient and often faster coordination for complex/reconstructive work.
- University dental clinic (University of Colorado School of Dental Medicine)
  - Why: Faculty‑supervised residents often offer high-quality care at lower cost; good option if budget or access is a concern.

What to ask when you call (use for any practice)
- Credentials: Is the implant surgeon a Diplomate / board‑certified (ABOMS for oral surgeons, American Board of Periodontology, American Board of Prosthodontics) or a Fellow of implant organizations?
- Experience: How many implants do they place per month? Do they place the specific procedure you need (single implant, multiple implants, All‑on‑4)?
- Imaging & planning: Do they use CBCT/3D imaging and guided implant planning?
- On‑site capabilities: Do they do bone grafts, sinus lifts, sedation, and lab work on site?
- Implant systems: Which implant brands do they use (Nobel Biocare, Straumann, Zimmer, etc.) and why?
- Timeline & steps: How many visits and how long from placement to final crown?
- Costs & financing: Ask for a written estimate (separate line items: implant, abutment, crown, grafting, extractions) and whether they accept your insurance or offer payment plans/third‑party financing.
- Warranty & follow‑up: Do they offer a warranty on the implant/restoration and what follow‑up/maintenance is included?
- Before/after photos & references: Can they show cases like yours and provide patient reviews?

Typical cost ballpark (Denver area; get clinic quotes)
- Single implant + abutment + crown: commonly about $3,000–$6,000 (can be lower/higher)
- Bone grafting: $300–$2,000 (depends on extent and material)
- Sinus lift: $1,000–$3,000
- Full-arch solutions (All‑on‑4/All‑on‑6): $15,000–$35,000 per arch (wide variability)
(These are estimates—get a written estimate from any clinic.)

If you give me your ZIP code/neighborhood and any preferences (insurance, budget, sedation), I’ll list 4–6 specific Denver practices to call and explain why each is a good fit for your situation.
